intro: In 2014, Pakistan skipped straight past the mobile-broadband queue — here's how a single spectrum auction reshaped how the country goes online.

facts.heading: The 2014 Spectrum Auction
facts.detail: Pakistan's first spectrum auction for mobile broadband raised $1.1 billion combined ($903 million from the 2100MHz band, $210 million from 1800MHz). Zong, Mobilink, Telenor, and Ufone won 3G licenses; Zong alone won 4G.

facts.heading: Rollout Obligations
facts.detail: Winning operators were required to bring 3G coverage to Islamabad, Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta, and 10 more cities within 6 months, and to 80% of district headquarters within 18 months.

facts.heading: A Second Round (2016)
facts.detail: A follow-up spectrum auction in 2016 saw Telenor secure an additional 4G license, further expanding network coverage.

facts.heading: Looking to 5G
facts.detail: By early 2017, 3G/4G subscribers had reached 37 million. In 2019, Pakistan became the first South Asian country to test 5G mobile network services.
facts.source: ProPakistani — Launch of 3G/4G Services in Pakistan

facts.heading: Economic Ripple Effect
facts.detail: By 2023, an estimated 200,000 direct and indirect jobs had been created by the telecom sector as a result of network expansion since the 2014 auction.
facts.source: ProPakistani — Launch of 3G/4G Services Created 0.2 Million Jobs
